site.name: Game Discovery Engine
site.description: Find your next game by the qualities that actually matter — tone, mechanics, aesthetic, and structure — not by genre tags.

games.title: Hollow Knight
games.summary: A lone knight descends into the ruined, insect-ridden kingdom of Hallownest, mapping a vast interconnected underworld and unraveling the quiet catastrophe that hollowed it out.
games.tagline: A hand-drawn descent into a hollowed kingdom.

characteristics.name: Metroidvania
characteristics.rationale: One continuous ability-gated map that rewards patient backtracking.

characteristics.name: Melancholic
characteristics.rationale: A dying kingdom rendered with restrained, mournful atmosphere.

characteristics.name: Painterly
characteristics.rationale: Hand-drawn, ink-and-watercolour environments.

characteristics.name: Permadeath
characteristics.rationale: Death drops your currency at the spot you fell, echoing soulslike stakes.

sections.heading: A kingdom you learn by heart
sections.prose: Hallownest is not a level list; it is a place. Rooms connect to rooms connect to the ability that finally lets you reach the ledge you noticed three hours ago. The map is deliberately withheld until you find a hunched cartographer humming in the dark, so early exploration has the genuine unease of being lost somewhere old and large.

sections.heading: Grief in a minor key
sections.prose: The tone never raises its voice. NPCs sit alone in ruined benches, remembering. The soundtrack thins to a single piano line. Hollow Knight trusts silence and restraint to carry its sadness, which is why the rare swell of music lands so hard.

sections.heading: Precision under the ink
sections.prose: Beneath the mood is a taut action game. Nail strikes, pogo bounces, and charm loadouts turn combat into a build-craft puzzle, and the optional challenge arenas are as demanding as anything in the genre.

games.title: Disco Elysium
games.summary: A detective wakes with no memory and a ruined city outside the window. Solve a murder — or don't — while the warring voices in your own head argue over who you are.
games.tagline: A murder mystery argued by the voices in your skull.

characteristics.name: Existential
characteristics.rationale: The plot is a scaffold for questions of failure, ideology, and self.

characteristics.name: Melancholic
characteristics.rationale: A hungover city of faded revolutions and personal wreckage.

characteristics.name: Painterly
characteristics.rationale: Oil-painted portraits and environments in a deliberately smeared style.

characteristics.name: Immersive Sim
characteristics.rationale: Skills act as systemic actors, opening many dialogue-driven paths.

sections.heading: Your mind is the level design
sections.prose: There is barely any combat. The real world is your own psyche: twenty-four skills that speak up unbidden, flatter you, lie to you, and occasionally solve the case. Building a character here means deciding which internal voices get to be loud.

sections.heading: A city with a hangover
sections.prose: Revachol is a place where a revolution already failed and everyone is living in the debris. The writing is unafraid of politics, grief, and embarrassment, and it lets you be a genuinely broken person without flinching.

sections.heading: Painted like a memory
sections.prose: Every portrait looks half-remembered, brushstrokes left visible, colours bruised. The art doesn't illustrate the world so much as recall it, which suits a game entirely about an unreliable narrator.

games.title: Hades
games.summary: The son of Hades fights his way up out of the Underworld, dying, returning, and dying again — and every death is another conversation with the family he's trying to escape.
games.tagline: Die, chat with the gods, run it back.

characteristics.name: Run-Based
characteristics.rationale: Discrete escape attempts with meta-progression between them.

characteristics.name: Permadeath
characteristics.rationale: Each death resets the run but advances the story.

characteristics.name: Painterly
characteristics.rationale: Lush comic-book character art and vivid god portraits.

characteristics.name: Cozy
characteristics.rationale: The hub becomes a warm, gossipy home you return to between runs.

sections.heading: Death as a narrative engine
sections.prose: Most roguelikes treat dying as a reset. Hades treats it as a scene transition. Fail, and you're pulled back to the House of Hades where your father needles you, the staff catch you up, and new dialogue unlocks. The loop and the story are the same loop.

sections.heading: Build variety with personality
sections.prose: Boons come from named gods with opinions, so assembling a run feels like brokering favours rather than picking from a menu. The synergy space is deep enough to chase for hundreds of hours.

sections.heading: A home worth escaping to
sections.prose: For a game about clawing out of hell, Hades is remarkably warm. The hub fills with relationships, and "one more run" is often about who you'll talk to when you inevitably fail.

games.title: Celeste
games.summary: A young woman climbs a haunted mountain and, in the process, climbs out of her own anxiety. A razor-precise platformer wrapped around a tender story about panic and persistence.
games.tagline: Climb the mountain, and the panic inside it.

characteristics.name: Pixel Art
characteristics.rationale: Crisp, expressive pixel work with a strong colour identity.

characteristics.name: Existential
characteristics.rationale: A literal ascent standing in for a struggle with the self.

characteristics.name: Permadeath
characteristics.rationale: Instant restarts make death frictionless rather than punishing.

characteristics.name: Melancholic
characteristics.rationale: Gentle sadness threaded through an ultimately hopeful arc.

sections.heading: Precision without cruelty
sections.prose: Celeste is brutally hard and completely kind about it. You die instantly and respawn instantly, so a screen becomes a phrase you rehearse until it's music. The difficulty is real; the friction is engineered away.

sections.heading: The mountain is a metaphor, and it knows
sections.prose: The climb externalises Madeline's anxiety into a character she has to reckon with rather than defeat. It's earnest without being saccharine, and the platforming difficulty becomes part of the point.

sections.heading: Pixels with a pulse
sections.prose: The pixel art is small but enormously expressive — a hair colour that reads as a mechanic, a palette that shifts with the mountain's mood. Every chapter feels visually distinct.

games.title: Outer Wilds
games.summary: You are a new astronaut in a tiny hand-built solar system caught in a twenty-two minute time loop. The only progression is what you understand.
games.tagline: A solar system that only unlocks in your head.

characteristics.name: Existential
characteristics.rationale: A meditation on endings staged as a physics-driven mystery.

characteristics.name: Immersive Sim
characteristics.rationale: A fully simulated system where knowledge, not items, is the key.

characteristics.name: Open World
characteristics.rationale: Every planet is reachable from minute one; order is yours to choose.

characteristics.name: Melancholic
characteristics.rationale: A wistful warmth about impermanence hums under the exploration.

sections.heading: Progress is understanding
sections.prose: There are no upgrades. Your ship at hour twenty is identical to hour one. The only thing that changes is you — what you've pieced together about the loop, the Nomai, and the quiet catastrophe underneath it all. It is the purest knowledge-gated game ever made.

sections.heading: A cosmos you can hold
sections.prose: The solar system is small enough to feel personal and simulated enough to surprise you: sand drains between twin planets, a black hole waits where you didn't expect one. Physics is the puzzle designer.

sections.heading: Tender about the end of things
sections.prose: Beneath the mystery is a gentle, unflinching thesis about endings. It earns its final act by making twenty-two minutes feel like a whole life, over and over.

games.title: Slay the Spire
games.summary: Climb a shifting tower one card-driven combat at a time, building a deck out of the spoils and praying your synergies hold together before the boss does.
games.tagline: One tower, a thousand decks, no two the same.

characteristics.name: Deckbuilding
characteristics.rationale: The defining deckbuilding roguelike; every fight reshapes your deck.

characteristics.name: Run-Based
characteristics.rationale: Discrete tower ascents with unlocks between attempts.

characteristics.name: Permadeath
characteristics.rationale: A loss ends the run; the deck you built dies with it.

characteristics.name: Cozy
characteristics.rationale: The systemic calm of an endlessly replayable puzzle box.

sections.heading: Every card is a decision that compounds
sections.prose: Slay the Spire's genius is that a good card early can be a bad card later. Adding to your deck dilutes it; the whole game is a running argument between power and consistency. It reads like a puzzle you assemble while playing it.

sections.heading: The tower reshuffles the stakes
sections.prose: Branching paths let you weigh risk against reward — elites for relics, rests for healing, unknowns for chaos. Meta-unlocks slowly widen the card pool, so the hundredth run still shows you something new.

sections.heading: A quiet, endless puzzle box
sections.prose: There's no story to speak of and that's the point. It's a systemic calm you can sink into for years, the kind of game that becomes a permanent tab in your life.
